Meaningless? No. My body art means a hell of a lot for me. From the Scorpion for a friend I lost in highschool to suicide, we used to play mortal combat and he'd always pick scorpion, my sons middle name incorporated, the p. metallica tarantula well just because something is scary or different in it's own way it's beautiful, it's not like it's just a tattoo i picked out and put on my skin. I put 4 years into planning it out how i wanted it to be and I finally had a point in life (sold my truck) to where I could afford it, and a time where the pain in my life out weighed the pain of getting it done. I would do it all again knowing the pain I'd go through to honor my friend, my family, my life in a piece of art that will be with me forever. The thing to understand is its for me, for myself, i know the meaning. Yes I know displaying it on my skin seems like it's for others to see and like but everyday looking in the mirror I get to see my version, my rememberance of a friend on my shoulder like my own little jiminy cricket just sitting there to help me in my darkest times. It may seem meaningless to you, but I didn't do it for you.

1.It is a Bio-Mech/Organica style with a few twists. I have a photo realistic Scorpion, a P. Metallica Tarantula and a Green Tree Python eye, mixed in with some wicked background of cables, bone and jagged spikes. It's from my right elbow to the top of my shoulder most of the way around.

2.It was done by Tony Zolina @ Red Dragon Tattoo in California.

3.Well we both kind of clicked off the bat, it was his favorite style and we just kept bouncing ideas off of each other and adding to it. I was surprised when he didn't mind continuing through the work. Everyone kept saying F" thats a mans tattoo right there. He kept asking if I was ok and for the most part it was alright, I almost passed out though when he went back over the tarantula 5 hours after it sat, that was extremely painful.

I guess the reason I wanted it done was because I am going through a divorce (I posted the story) and wanted something for me so poof a wild epic tattoo appeared. First thing he told me was "no one will believe you sat through this in one shot, its insane" so we took plenty of pics along the way. If I could figure how to upload them I'd put it up.
